bones.name: l_tarsal_distal_phalanx_1
bones.function: Distal (ungual) phalanx of the great toe. Its broad base articulates directly with the proximal phalanx (the great toe has no middle phalanx), and its expanded distal extremity supports the nail and the end of the toe.
bones.note: The great toe has no middle phalanx: Gray counts two phalanges in the great toe and three in each of the other toes.
bones.source: grays1918:ungual phalanges, in form, resemble those of the fingers

bones.name: l_tarsal_distal_phalanx_2
bones.function: Distal (ungual) phalanx of the second toe. Gray notes the ungual phalanges of the foot resemble those of the fingers in form, but are smaller and flattened from above downward; each presents a broad base for articulation with the corresponding bone of the second row, and an expanded distal extremity for the support of the nail and end of the toe.
bones.note: Gray notes each phalanx of the foot ossifies from two centers — one for the body (appearing about the tenth week) and one for the base (fourth to tenth year), which joins the body about the eighteenth year.
bones.source: grays1918:ungual phalanges, in form, resemble those of the fingers

bones.name: l_tarsal_proximal_phalanx_1
bones.function: Proximal phalanx of the great toe. Its concave base receives the head of the first metatarsal, and its head presents a trochlear surface for the distal phalanx — the great toe has only two phalanges, so this row articulates directly with the ungual phalanx.

synonyms: first phalanx of the great toe (hallux)
bones.source: grays1918:two in the great toe, and three in each

bones.source: grays1918:base is concave; and the head presents a trochlear surface
